criteria.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies that Disclosure Schedule 3.9 lists only 12 patents, not 14
criteria.reasoning: The memo states that Schedule 3.9(a) lists 12 issued U.S. patents and that diligence identified two additional issued patents directly related to the PF-4200 valve that were omitted. This identifies the two-patent discrepancy and necessarily reflects 14 issued patents in diligence.

criteria.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies the omitted patents as U.S. Patent Nos. 10,891,234 and 10,891,235
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies two omitted issued patents related to the PF-4200 proportional valve but does not specify their patent numbers, U.S. Patent Nos. 10,891,234 and 10,891,235.

criteria.title: ISSUE_001: Links omitted patents to PF-4200 valve and AquaDyne dispute
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the omitted patents as relating to the PF-4200 proportional valve and separately discusses the AquaDyne cease-and-desist dispute, but it does not state that AquaDyne accused the PF-4200 product or connect the omitted patents to that infringement claim. Therefore, it does not satisfy the criterion.

criteria.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies caveat in AquaDyne non-infringement opinion re claim 14
criteria.reasoning: The memo notes that the AquaDyne non-infringement opinion is incomplete because the Target refused to provide internal testing data, but it does not specifically identify the unanalysed claim 14 of U.S. Patent No. 11,234,567 or name Hargrove & Lind LLP. The required caveat is therefore not fully identified.

criteria.title: ISSUE_002: Flags that SPA IP representation omits the claim 14 caveat from the non-infringement opinion
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies incomplete AquaDyne non-infringement support and notes that Target withheld testing data, but it does not mention the specific claim 14 caveat or expressly connect that limitation to a deficiency in the SPA's non-infringement representation.

criteria.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies NorthPoint Fabrication MSA expired before SPA signing
criteria.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies the NorthPoint Fabrication MSA as expired on February 28, 2025, states that it had not been renewed, and classifies the issue as a critical discrepancy. It therefore satisfies the criterion, including the fact that the expiration preceded the March 14, 2025 SPA signing date.

criteria.title: ISSUE_003: Flags conflict with SPA rep that contracts are 'in full force and effect'
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies that the NorthPoint MSA expired and had not been renewed, but it does not expressly state that this conflicts with the SPA representation that listed material contracts are 'in full force and effect,' nor does it note the parties' informal performance.

criteria.title: ISSUE_003: Notes NorthPoint revenue concentration risk ($18.6M / 13%)
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies NorthPoint as associated with approximately $18.6 million of annual revenue and explains the material revenue and contract-continuity risk, satisfying the criterion.

criteria.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies Kessler MSA change-of-control clause not disclosed in Schedule 3.15
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the undisclosed Kessler change-of-control right, states that the Kessler Heavy Industries MSA contains an undisclosed change-of-control termination right, and notes its material revenue significance. It therefore satisfies the criterion, although it references SPA §3.16 and the material-contract schedule rather than specifically Schedule 3.15 and does not state the 60-day notice period.

criteria.title: ISSUE_004: Notes Kessler is largest customer with ~$29.4M / ~20.6% of revenue
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies Kessler Heavy Industries and states that it represents approximately 20.6% of Company revenue, while flagging the post-closing termination risk. However, it does not identify Kessler as the Target’s largest customer. Because that element is expressly required, the criterion is not fully satisfied.

criteria.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies Phase I REC not disclosed in environmental Schedule 3.12
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the omitted Dayton environmental condition, states that a Phase I assessment found a separate recognized environmental condition, and contrasts it with Schedule 3.12, which only discloses the July 2023 hydraulic-fluid spill. Although it does not specify the October 2024 Greenleaf assessment or historical solvent contamination from a prior tenant, it identifies the material undisclosed REC required by the criterion.

criteria.title: ISSUE_005: Notes Phase II investigation has not been completed
criteria.reasoning: The memo explicitly states under the Dayton environmental condition that no Phase II investigation has been completed, and recommends commissioning one to assess the identified environmental condition.

criteria.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies California tax nexus — no returns filed despite nexus
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies an unreported California physical presence, approximately $3.8 million in California-sourced sales, and no California returns filed since at least 2022. It expressly maps this to SPA §3.14 and notes the resulting conflict and potential tax exposure.

criteria.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies questionable COVID supply chain EBITDA adjustment ($0.60M)
criteria.reasoning: The memo questions the $0.60 million COVID-related EBITDA add-back and identifies approximately $0.38 million as recurring, but it does not mention the prior-year comparable charges of approximately $0.45 million in FY2023 and $0.55 million in FY2022 or otherwise note that historical repetition supports treating the adjustment as recurring.

criteria.title: ISSUE_007: Calculates purchase price impact of COVID add-back (~$5.7M at 9.5x)
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the $0.60 million COVID-related charge but calculates only the $0.38 million recurring portion at approximately $3.61 million using the 9.5x multiple. It does not calculate or reference the required total $5.7 million purchase price impact ($0.60 million × 9.5).

criteria.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies pension unfunded liability discrepancy ($4.3M vs. ~$6.8M)
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the pension discrepancy, stating that the SPA/disclosures do not fully reflect the updated obligation and that updated actuarial assumptions show the unfunded liability is understated by approximately $2.5 million. It also recommends obtaining the updated actuarial report and reconciling the liability. Although it does not expressly state the underlying $4.3 million versus approximately $6.8 million figures or mention declining interest rates, it identifies the required $2.5 million discrepancy and its material implications.

criteria.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies $2M insurance gap in Martinez litigation and conflict with SPA insurance rep
criteria.reasoning: The memo correctly identifies the $12 million Martinez demand, the $10 million per-occurrence policy limit, and the resulting potential $2 million coverage gap. However, it does not expressly identify that this shortfall conflicts with the SPA representation that all litigation is covered by insurance.

criteria.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies Monterrey lease COC consent not on Required Consents schedule
criteria.reasoning: The memo does not identify the Monterrey facility lease with Inmobiliaria del Norte, S.A. de C.V., its landlord-consent requirement for a direct or indirect change of control, the indirect change of control resulting from the acquisition, or the omission from SPA Schedule 5.3.

criteria.title: ISSUE_010: Notes Monterrey facility revenue significance (~$38.2M / ~26.7%)
criteria.reasoning: The memo does not mention the Monterrey facility or its operational significance, including approximately $38.2 million in revenue or 26.7% of total revenue.

criteria.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies employee count discrepancy (730 in schedule vs. 740 actual)
criteria.reasoning: The memo includes a generic employment/benefit disclosure mismatch but does not identify the specific discrepancy: Disclosure Schedule 3.17 lists 730 employees versus 740 in the diligence/HR data, a difference of 10 employees apparently attributable to Q4 2024 Monterrey hires.

criteria.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies IRC § 382 limitation on NOL carryforwards post-acquisition
criteria.reasoning: The memo discusses California tax nexus and unfiled returns but does not identify the Target's $4.1 million federal NOL carryforwards or explain that the 100% stock acquisition triggers an ownership change subject to IRC § 382 annual-use limitations.

criteria.title: ISSUE_012: Notes that the SPA does not address IRC § 382 NOL limitation
criteria.reasoning: The memo does not mention IRC § 382, the limitation on NOL carryforwards, or the SPA's failure to address or disclose that limitation.

criteria.title: ISSUE_013: Identifies contested OSHA citation conflicts with compliance rep
criteria.reasoning: The memo does not identify or discuss the October 2024 OSHA lockout/tagout citation, its $28,700 penalty, its contested status, or the conflict with the SPA compliance representation that governmental orders, penalties, and citations are fully resolved and/or that the Target is in material compliance with applicable laws.

criteria.title: ISSUE_014: Identifies Karen Beecham disputed share claim as title encumbrance
criteria.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies the disputed Karen Beecham share interest as a CRITICAL issue. It states that the 2021 divorce/property settlement may encumber approximately 3.1% of outstanding shares and describes the resulting potential title defect. It also directly cites the SPA's good and marketable title representation, free of encumbrances, and recommends obtaining a release or making clean title a closing condition.

criteria.title: Each issue includes severity rating (Critical/High/Medium)
criteria.reasoning: All 11 identified discrepancies include an explicit tiered severity label: Critical, High, or Medium. This exceeds the 75% threshold.

criteria.title: Each issue cites specific SPA section and diligence source documents
criteria.reasoning: FAIL. Although all 11 discrepancies identify specific SPA sections or disclosure schedules, only the AquaDyne issue expressly names a diligence source document (the IP diligence memo). The other issues generally refer to 'diligence,' an assessment, or an updated bridge without identifying a source document by name, and the global sources list is not mapped to individual discrepancies. This is well below the 75% threshold.

criteria.title: Each issue includes recommended next steps
criteria.reasoning: All 11 identified discrepancies include specific recommended next steps, such as correcting disclosure schedules, obtaining consents or waivers, conducting additional diligence, securing specific indemnities or escrow, making closing conditions, filing tax returns, and adjusting purchase price or EBITDA. This exceeds the 75% threshold.

criteria.title: Correctly references SPA signing date of March 14, 2025
criteria.reasoning: The memo does not expressly state the SPA signing date, but its discussion of the NorthPoint MSA expiring on February 28, 2025 and requiring renewal before signing is consistent with a March 14, 2025 signing date. It contains no conflicting date.

criteria.title: Correctly identifies purchase price as $287 million
criteria.reasoning: The memo does not identify the aggregate purchase price as $287 million. It instead references an implied value of approximately $283.4 million and a potential price effect of approximately $3.61 million.

criteria.title: ISSUE_006: Recommends action such as voluntary disclosure or indemnity for CA tax
criteria.reasoning: The memo specifically addresses the California income-tax nexus and unfiled returns, recommending a state-tax nexus/liability analysis, registration, filing or amendment of delinquent returns, and a specific tax indemnity outside the general basket/cap with tax escrow or withholding if material.

criteria.title: ISSUE_005: Recommends Phase II environmental investigation
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the Dayton environmental condition and expressly recommends commissioning a Phase II investigation or qualified risk assessment, along with a specific environmental indemnity and dedicated escrow.

criteria.title: ISSUE_014: Notes potential impact on closing or need for resolution
criteria.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies the Karen Beecham share claim as CRITICAL and states it creates a potential title defect, ownership challenge, voting/closing impediment, and litigation risk. It recommends resolving the issue before closing by obtaining a release or waiver, adding Karen as a party, making clean title a closing condition, or using dedicated escrow and indemnity protection. The executive action plan also calls for resolving the claim and obtaining clean title before signing.

criteria.title: ISSUE_008: Recommends updated actuarial valuation or purchase price adjustment
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the approximately $2.5 million pension underfunding discrepancy and recommends obtaining the updated actuarial report, reconciling the liability, and requiring a balance-sheet adjustment or price reduction, along with a specific indemnity.

criteria.title: ISSUE_004: Recommends obtaining Kessler consent or waiver pre-closing
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the undisclosed Kessler change-of-control termination right as CRITICAL and expressly recommends obtaining written consent or waiver before signing/closing, making it a closing condition, and adding specific indemnity and price/escrow protection.

criteria.title: ISSUE_009: Correctly calculates insurance gap as $2M ($12M claim minus $10M limit)
criteria.reasoning: The memo correctly calculates and identifies the Martinez insurance coverage gap as approximately $2 million, based on the approximately $12 million demand exceeding the $10 million per-occurrence policy limit.

criteria.title: ISSUE_001: Recommends updating Schedule 3.9 to include all 14 patents
criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies the two omitted PF-4200 patents and expressly recommends correcting Schedule 3.9(a) to include them, along with confirming ownership, inventors, jurisdictions, maintenance status, liens/licenses, and chain of title. This satisfies the requirement to update the IP schedule to include all 14 issued patents.

criteria.title: ISSUE_002: Recommends requesting full testing data or supplemental opinion
criteria.reasoning: The memo expressly recommends producing the withheld internal testing data, communications, claim charts, and counsel opinion; obtaining an updated independent non-infringement opinion; and adding a specific indemnity for the AquaDyne claim. This directly satisfies the criterion.

criteria.title: Identifies at least 10 of the 14 planted issues
criteria.reasoning: PASS. The memo identifies at least 10 planted issues: omitted PF-4200 patents; incomplete AquaDyne non-infringement support; expired NorthPoint contract; undisclosed Kessler change-of-control right; omitted Dayton Phase I recognized environmental condition; California tax nexus and unfiled returns; questionable COVID EBITDA add-back; understated pension liability; Martinez insurance gap; and the Karen Beecham disputed share claim. It does not identify the Monterrey lease consent, employee-count discrepancy, IRC § 382 limitation, or OSHA citation, but it exceeds the 10-issue threshold.
